::: {#exr-miller-taylor-cos-cubed}
#### Taylor series of a power of a function

Adapted from @problifesavercalc, Question 1.1.19.

Find the terms up to degree 4 in the Taylor series for

$$f(x) = \cos^3(5x)$$

at $x_0 = 0$.
:::

::: {#sol-miller-taylor-cos-cubed}
From @exr-miller-taylor-cos-scaled, the expansion of $\cos(5x)$ up to order $x^4$ is:

$$\cos(5x) = 1 - \frac{25}{2}x^2 + \frac{625}{24}x^4 + O(x^6)$$

Cube this expansion using $(1 - y)^3 = 1 - 3y + 3y^2 - y^3$ with $y = \frac{25}{2}x^2 - \frac{625}{24}x^4$:

$$\ba
\cos^3(5x) &= 1 - 3\paren{\frac{25}{2}x^2 - \frac{625}{24}x^4} + 3\paren{\frac{25}{2}x^2}^2 + O(x^6)
\\
&= 1 - \frac{75}{2}x^2 + \frac{625}{8}x^4 + \frac{1875}{4}x^4 + O(x^6)
\\
&= 1 - \frac{75}{2}x^2 + \frac{4375}{8}x^4 + O(x^6)
\ea$$
:::
